avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, and the fight against emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and pays for them to be planted on sidewalks, in parks and on private land. It also funds the machinery and the teams of employees who do this work in the boroughs. At the same time, some borough councils are allowing construction projects to depart from the rules on trees and greening.

etapes.titre: Contracts for planting trees on public land
etapes.texte: City council awards two contracts to supply and plant 1,374 trees in seven boroughs, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expenditure is $2,456,590.55, taxes included.

The City is paying $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional land until December 31, 2026. Pierrefonds-Roxboro is separately transferring $162,233.12 from its parks fund to buy trees and plants.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an extension on rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is renting a mini-backhoe with operator for $152,916.75 and setting aside $200,000 for blue-collar teams assigned to planting. Outremont is awarding the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting vegetation, for an expenditure of $800,416.17, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

etapes.titre: Land leased for a tree nursery
etapes.texte: The City is leasing lots in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for $100, so that it can operate a transition tree nursery there. The lease runs for 24 months starting May 1, 2026, and the property subsidy is estimated at $329,600.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit a progress report by October 31, 2026, its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its summary and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The 855 trees in lot 2 must be planted in spring 2027; watering, maintenance and replacement continue until the end of November 2029.
The lease for the transition tree nursery ends on April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.titre: Spring cleaning of streets and sidewalks
etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini-sweeper with operators to remove abrasives from streets, lanes, sidewalks and bike paths. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing an expenditure of $574,920.99, taxes included, for this purpose for 2026 and 2027 [CA26 27 0008].

etapes.titre: Snow removal from downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is entrusting companies with the maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal of Square Viger and Place des Montréalaises, as well as square Dorchester, place du Canada, îlot Bonaventure, square Victoria, place du Sable-Gris and square Chaboillez. The borough is also extending by one year the snow removal of the Quartier des Spectacles, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

City council is awarding turnkey snow removal contracts covering four winter seasons in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Sud-Ouest, as well as a five-season contract for Plateau-Mont-Royal, worth $22,042,432.13, taxes included [CM26 1013]. Other contracts cover towing in Montréal-Nord, the rental of equipment with operators in Saint-Laurent and snow removal from the roads and parking lots of the Grand parc de l'Ouest.

The City is hiring companies to haul snow in sectors cleared by its own crews, to rent equipment with operators in Plateau-Mont-Royal and to tow vehicles during operations. Boroughs are also renting graders and loader-tractors for the winter, and Ville-Marie is entrusting the snow removal of the esplanade du Champ-de-Mars and the city hall stairs.

aSurveiller.texte: The turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.
The turnkey snow removal contract for Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031.
Snow removal from the roads and parking lots of the Grand parc de l'Ouest runs from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Towing related to snow removal in Plateau-Mont-Royal is scheduled from November 15, 2026 to March 31, 2027.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and launching work on its water networks: rehabilitation of secondary pipes in about fifteen boroughs, reconstruction of main pipes on streets downtown, and replacement of lead water service connections. It is also continuing the disinfection project at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant and awarding maintenance and construction contracts there. Several loan by-laws and a request for financial assistance to the Québec government govern the funding of this work.

etapes.titre: Increase in the loan for disinfection
etapes.texte: The City is raising from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000 the loan funding the disinfection unit for the effluent at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. The money is used to finish the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks, and build the oxygen production plant.

The City is awarding a series of contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes without trenching and redo the roadway, on streets in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve and other sectors. This work includes replacing lead water service connections, on both the public and private sides.

The City is awarding contracts to rebuild water pipes and infrastructure along rue Guy, between Saint-Jacques and René-Lévesque, and on rue De Champlain, between Sainte-Catherine Est and René-Lévesque. It is also adding funds to ongoing contracts, including the rehabilitation of a pipe under rue de la Cathédrale, up to the McTavish reservoir, and completed work on rue Saint-Antoine Ouest.

etapes.titre: Loans and request for financial assistance
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council is adopting a $12,000,000 loan for main pipes in the Namur–De la Savane sector, and the city council is adopting a $951,000,000 loan for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks. The City is authorizing a request for financial assistance under the PRIMEAU program for the main network and the wastewater treatment plant, and is filing a $313,000,000 loan project for the main waterworks network.

aSurveiller.texte: Adoption expected on November 16, 2026 of the by-law amending the rules on waterworks and sewer connections and stormwater management (20-030).
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 4 at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant in January 2027, for about six weeks of work.
Completion of the rehabilitation work on the rue de la Cathédrale pipe pushed back to March 2027.
Rue Guy project expected to continue until December 2027.
Commissioning of the ozone plant expected in 2029, with contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 set to end in the last quarter of 2028.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump site, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is continuing development of parc Frédéric-Back, on the site of the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel. It is approving construction of a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood and assigning its delivery to the arrondissement de Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. It is also awarding contracts for park maintenance, electrical work on the site and the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, and seeking financial assistance from Québec and Canada.

etapes.titre: Funding request for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking Québec's ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for assistance of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre trail crossing the park from east to west, with a footbridge about 150 metres long [CG26 0121]. This link will connect two neighbourhoods that have until now been separated by the former quarry.

The City is approving a greenhouse complex in the southwest sector of the park: 1,500 m² for research and training, 1,000 m² for the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, at an estimated cost of $2,185,000 [CG26 0124]. The arrondissement de Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is offering to carry out the project and city council is accepting.

The City is assigning general upkeep and ecological and horticultural management of the park to two companies for 30 months, from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028 [CG26 0224]. It is also awarding a contract for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel: a new 25 kV power supply, transformer, backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture.

The borough is awarding a contract worth $8,199,514.82, taxes included, to redevelop rue De Louvain between the park and boulevard Saint-Michel: sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, cycling facilities and plantings [CA26 14 0076]. In October, it is authorizing a funding request to the Véloce III program for the bike lane and sidewalks.

The City is extending by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator on the site; the compost is used, among other things, for developing the park [CG26 0320]. The borough is then awarding a contract worth $499,865.92, taxes included, for the supply and installation of two greenhouses [CA26 14 0163].

The City is extending snow removal at the park, the TAZ and the soccer stadium by six months [CG26 0521]. It is also authorizing a request to Canada's Natural Infrastructure Fund and approving the contribution agreement for development of the park, whose total cost is estimated at $25,156,849, taxes included [CG26 0616].

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the TAPU program, for which the City is seeking assistance for the footbridge and the east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Completion of the greenhouse installation work is scheduled for December 2026, with commissioning planned for winter 2027.
Snow removal for the park, the TAZ and the soccer stadium is covered from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
According to the maintenance file, 26 more hectares will be added to the park in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, in the process of being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.
grand-parc-ouest.enBref: This year, the City is maintaining and protecting the sectors of the Grand parc de l'Ouest. It adjusted a contract for the repair of heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, submitted an application for an international designation related to night skies at Cap-Saint-Jacques, and had two sectors listed in a registry of protected natural environments. It also awarded contracts for culvert reconstruction, snow removal, tree felling and housekeeping.

etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. Buried stones, extra mortar and a deteriorated culvert account for the increase, according to file 1255414002.

The City submits the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector (330 hectares) for the Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. It commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping nighttime access open to the public.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector (429 ha) are listed in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité, with conservation plans. Elected officials also receive the 2025 report on the areas.

The City awards contracts for snow removal on the service roads and parking lots of Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques, as well as housekeeping for nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques, including the welcome chalet, Maison Richer and Château Gohier.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028, with no possible extension.
Housekeeping of the nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
Tree felling planned from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
For the night sky designation: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, DarkSky's response expected in April 2027, site compliance by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations so they can open warming centres, and funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also sends a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness work related to homelessness, and signs contracts for support toward shelter and housing, particularly near encampments. It has set up a framework to receive private donations for these initiatives.

etapes.titre: Loan of buildings for warming centres
etapes.texte: The City is lending three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis, at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert, to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. All three loans run until April 30, 2026.

etapes.titre: Warming centres and outreach workers paid by the boroughs
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville raises to $126,615.07, taxes included, the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for operating a warming centre for winter 2025-2026. Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two outreach workers in its facilities, and Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the fit-out work of the Bain Saint-Denis warming centre.

etapes.titre: Shuttles, encampments and Nuit des sans-abri
etapes.texte: The City adds $860,692 to the three shuttle services run by Projets Autochtones du Québec, Mission Old Brewery and L'Amour en action Syl Dan, and extends their agreements to December 31, 2027. It awards seven contracts totalling $3,025,000, taxes included, for the Programme d'interventions spécialisées en campement, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026 to 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri.

aSurveiller.texte: The agreements for the three shuttle services are extended until December 31, 2027.
Support for organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs covers a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.
The seven contracts under the Programme d'interventions spécialisées en campement end on December 31, 2029.
The agreement on the public works team accepted by Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs from May 15, 2026 to May 15, 2027.

logement.description: Grants, land and social, affordable or student housing projects, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.

etapes.texte: City council approves the SHDM's 2026 budget, which provides for a budgeted surplus of $4.4M and a 2026-2028 capital program of $416.8M gross. The urban agglomeration council and city council approve the OMHM's 2026 budget, which goes from $541M in 2025 to $605.6M in 2026.

etapes.titre: Land obtained and transferred for social housing
etapes.texte: The City accepts from the Government of Canada half the rights to a 3,658.8 square-metre plot of land on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, at no cost. It also transfers, free of charge, to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni a 789.6 square-metre plot of land at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, and authorizes a devaluation of $110,000.

The City signs two 2025-2026 funding agreements with the Société d'habitation du Québec for temporary shelter and housing search assistance, including $500,000 for the OMHM's service. Following a public consultation held on February 26, 2026, city council amends by-law 20-041: it now only applies to projects larger than 18,000 square metres and imposes a single requirement of 20% non-market housing.

The City pays $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project, an additional $877,312 to Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, $25,110,800 to the Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel for 350 affordable housing units, and $13,151,528 to Immobilier collectif – Point commun for 395 housing units in Pointe-Saint-Charles. The executive committee authorizes the SHDM to build a 72-unit building on 2e Avenue, in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.

etapes.titre: Land purchases and right of first refusal
etapes.texte: The City buys a 1,535.1 square-metre plot of land near rues Chatham and William for $9,293,113, a 433.2 square-metre plot of land on rue de la Montagne for $500,000, and a 1,850 square-metre plot of land from the Molson site for $3,233,628, which it transfers free of charge to the SHDM. It removes lots in Ville-Marie and Le Sud-Ouest from the list of properties subject to the right of first refusal for social housing, and Saint-Laurent concludes a development agreement providing for a commitment to a social housing project on boulevard de la Côte-Vertu.

aSurveiller.texte: Ville-Marie plans to adopt, on November 10, 2026, its by-law amending temporary public domain occupancy fees for projects that include social, affordable or non-market housing.
Occupancy of the 350 affordable housing units at Technopôle Angus is expected no later than April 30, 2027.
Construction at 1685-1693, avenue de l'Église is to be completed in May 2027, and the building occupied in July 2027.
Work on the seniors' building in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles is to be completed in November 2027.
The Société de développement Écoquartier Louvain has until December 31, 2027, to make use of the $500,000 contribution.
Delivery of the 72-unit building on 2e Avenue is announced for May 2028, and occupancy of the 395-unit building in Pointe-Saint-Charles for February 2030.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: land acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.titre: Redevelopment of rue de Louvain Est
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82 including taxes [CA26 14 0076]. It then authorizes the filing of a financial assistance application to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for the bike lane and sidewalks.

etapes.titre: The central street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council names the new street at the heart of the Louvain eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Street, utility networks and soil in the eco-district
etapes.texte: The City awards Charex inc. the contract to build a street with sewer, water main, roadworks, lighting and environmental soil management in the Louvain eco-district, for a total expenditure of $15,366,336 including taxes. It adds $2,007,312.15 net, through the environmental liability reserve, to remediate the soil of the former gas station area on the Louvain Est site.

The borough gives $35,000 to Îlot 84 for the temporary space Esplanade - Louvain at 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, and authorizes an event-based and transitional use on the vacant lot at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest. It also adopts draft by-laws and a draft resolution to allow taller and denser buildings near avenue de l'Esplanade.

The City grants $500,000 to the Société de développement Écoquartier Louvain for studies and analyses prior to an off-market housing project. It also authorizes an additional expenditure of $48,398.55 to Loiselle inc. for sewer, water main and site preparation work related to the modular homes on the Louvain Ouest site.

aSurveiller.texte: Work on rue de Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The free loan of the land to the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine runs until October 31, 2027.
The Société de développement Écoquartier Louvain has until December 31, 2027 to make use of the $500,000 contribution.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collection, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is adjusting its collection rules in several boroughs, buying bins and extending contracts for processing food waste and transporting materials for ecocentres. It is also awarding hydro-excavation contracts with residual materials treatment in several boroughs. The 2025 residual materials management report and reports from the inspector general on collection subcontracting are being tabled at councils.

etapes.texte: The executive committee is changing collection days, schedules and sectors in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, where garbage is collected every two weeks from November 1 to April 30 and every week from May 1 to October 31. Two boroughs are also authorizing waste-related building arrangements: a storage room of at least 28 m² at 397 boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest, and an exemption from an outdoor drop-off area at 2380 rue Notre-Dame Ouest.

The City is extending its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. twice, by six months each time, to compost or biomethanize food waste from the eastern part of the agglomeration, at $3,269,055.43 taxes included per extension. It explains that the start-up of the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre is not confirmed and that it may end the contracts with 30 days' notice.

The City is entering into framework agreements to supply collection bins, including one with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins intended for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, where garbage collection will be spaced out. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is giving Ville en vert a mandate for information and awareness, and the executive committee is approving an agreement with Tricentris to lend reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

The City is extending the contract for supplying and transporting containers for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre, as well as the contracts for collecting garbage from front-loading and semi-underground containers. It is awarding Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25 taxes included, over 28 months, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs left at ecocentres.

aSurveiller.texte: The extension of the food waste processing contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The Saint-Laurent ecocentre container contract and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The discharge authorization management software contract covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets hippodrome: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the ground, literally and financially, for the future neighbourhood on the site of the former hippodrome. It obtained more time from Québec to sell a first piece of land, adopted two loan by-laws for waterworks and public domain, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for urban agriculture and a tree nursery.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City an extension until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The extension does not involve any financial compensation and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

The City guarantees a $2,000,000 loan granted by the Canada Infrastructure Bank to Société GALOPH, to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, city council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and management of the neighbourhood's public assets.

City council adopts a $29,000,000 loan to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, streets, fees and land purchases. The urban agglomeration council adopts a $12,000,000 loan to build main waterworks pipes between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella.

etapes.titre: Residential project approved on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough adopts a draft resolution authorizing four residential buildings in four phases at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur, including one housing a municipal sports and leisure centre. The borough secretary is tasked with holding a public consultation meeting.

etapes.titre: Land transferred to Communia and work paid for
etapes.texte: The City transfers, without financial compensation, a vacant 4,777.7 square metre lot in the southeast part of the site to Communia, for a non-market residential project of at least 225 housing units, and repeals the earlier agreement. It also pays $65,765.70 more to Loiselle inc. for sewer, waterworks and site preparation work related to the modular housing units.

aSurveiller.texte: October 31, 2027: deadline given by the Québec government to sell a first piece of land on the site.
April 30, 2027: end of MultiCaf's urban agriculture lease.
March 31, 2028: end of the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora's extended lease.
April 30, 2028: end of the lease for the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain's transitional tree nursery.
2031: deadline set by Ottawa to complete the infrastructure funded by its grant.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City is funding the design and redevelopment work for parks in several boroughs, from parc Le Prévost to parc Baldwin. It is also awarding maintenance and work contracts in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, and submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for an international dark sky designation. Several decisions adjust contracts already underway on park construction sites.

etapes.texte: The City is awarding the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expenditure of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It is also paying $174,471.56, net of taxes, to the arrondissement of Verdun for soil and environmental studies of parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, built on a former dump.

The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, having a culvert rebuilt under that same road, and awarding contracts for snow clearing of service roads and for felling ash trees and dying trees. It is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for Urban Night Sky Place designation and listing the Anse-à-l'Orme sector, along with the parc-nature des Sources, in the registry of protected natural areas.

Several decisions add money or shift budgets in projects already underway: construction supervision for parc du Bassin-à-Bois, parc des Hirondelles, parc du Sault-au-Récollet, parc Villeray, parc Percy-Walters, and the museography of parc des Sœurs de Sainte-Anne.

City council is removing a former 810.2 m² street section from the public domain as a street in order to add it to parc Campbell Ouest. It is doing the same with a 75.2 m² strip of laneway that crosses parc Le Prévost.

aSurveiller.texte: Completion of work at parc Denise-Morelle in November 2026, according to the file from the arrondissement of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
Snow clearing of the Grand parc de l'Ouest from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Housekeeping of nine buildings in the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
For the Cap-Saint-Jacques application: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site compliance work in April 2032.
Final acceptance of work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois expected in June 2027.
Completion of work at parc J.O.R.-Leduc in June 2028; tree felling in the Grand parc de l'Ouest until early summer 2028; installation of the artwork at parc des Eaux-Cachées in 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial activity by-laws.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is organizing the 2026 season of pedestrian streets and public squares: it is adopting funding rules, paying out money to boroughs and business development corporations, then closing street sections to cars and regulating sales, noise and traffic on these streets. It is also settling a dispute related to the development of a public square, changing the status of a piece of land, and naming a square.

etapes.titre: Funding rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre of pedestrianized street. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on a public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer.

Boroughs close sections to cars and authorize terraces, the sale of food and drinks, music, and street painting: Ville-Marie for thirteen streets, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce for the Placette CDN and avenues Royal and Madison, Outremont for avenue Bernard, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve for rue Ontario Est, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal for avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth.

The executive committee grants $40,000 to animate the Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street from July 10 to 19, 2026 during the FIFA World Cup. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce closes avenue de Monkland for a commercial promotion from August 20 to 23, 2026, and Ville-Marie authorizes a musical sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles.

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque, in Montréal-Nord, "place Chez-Marguerite", and changes a 899-square-metre piece of land from street status to local park status near the Langelier metro station. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal in three sections.

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Traffic resumes on the chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges ramp on November 1, 2026, after dismantling on November 1 and 2.
The by-law on the sound ambiance of the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transportation contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers the period until December 31, 2027; the 2027 edition takes place only if the pedestrianization project is renewed.
The pedestrianization assistance for avenue Lacombe continues until December 31, 2028: $22,500 in 2027 and $20,000 in 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is requesting an additional six months, after a first extension obtained in July 2025.

Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, Ville-Marie is revising its rules on urban planning, special projects, demolition, certificates and cadastral operations. The by-law authorizes a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and allows public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

The borough is changing heights, uses and the lot coverage ratio in the sector bordered by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est, and is increasing the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse. It is also amending its by-law on building demolition, following a public meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Laurent public consultation on its three draft by-laws, on October 20, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce: public consultation on October 21, 2026 and adoption on November 2, 2026; the deadline granted by the minister runs until December 16, 2026.
Saint-Léonard must adopt all its concordance by-laws by June 16, 2027, a date set by the Minister of Municipal Affairs.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting an extension until June 16, 2027.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.
L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

securite-publique.description: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: contracts, neighbourhood police stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to purchase and replace specialized SPVM equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a sergeant-detective to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

etapes.titre: Vehicles, buildings and new loan to the RCMP
etapes.texte: The City purchases 11 motorcycles for road patrol, extends janitorial services at headquarters by one year, and awards work to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building, at 1515 chemin Remembrance. It authorizes a second service loan to the RCMP starting March 30, 2026, with an additional budget of $136,260 for 2026.

The City purchases 3,000,000 practice cartridges of 9 mm calibre for firearms training, extends the internal courier service, and retains companies for carpentry and painting in SPVM buildings. It renews the lease for the neighbourhood police station 26, avenue Mountain Sights, and loans a police officer to the Sûreté du Québec team on exporting stolen vehicles.

aSurveiller.texte: The work to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building must be completed by September 30, 2027.
The patrol boat and its trailer must be delivered no later than March 1, 2027.
The lease for the metro unit premises at neighbourhood police station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, begins on February 1, 2027 and ends on January 31, 2037.
Maintenance of the SIGAL software is extended from January 1 to December 31, 2027.
The ACCES Tabac, Alcool, Cannabis and ACCEF teams are extended until March 31, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides about the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the budget and borrowings of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), and sells, leases or lends it land for its stations, ventilation plants and staff. It also oversees metro construction sites and bus stops on its territory, and entrusts the STM with municipal work related to the extension of the blue line. Borough councils and city council adopt motions on the development of the network.

etapes.titre: Bus stops and construction sites overseen
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville sets up and removes bus waiting posts as part of the network overhaul, and Saint-Laurent offers to take charge of building sidewalks at new stops. Ville-Marie authorizes the STM to drill and redo the vault of the green line tunnel 24 hours a day from June 10 to July 31, 2026; the City signs an agreement to build a pavilion attached to the Wiseman ventilation plant in Outremont, adds an incidental costs budget to the Berri-UQAM station construction site, and does not oppose the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel above the REM.

The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its own work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and authorizes an expenditure of $3,808,451.29, taxes included. It then enters into 72-month framework agreements with Artelia Canada inc. and Stantec Experts-conseils ltée for the design, technical assistance and impact management of the redevelopment of the blue line corridor.

The agglomeration approves STM borrowings and amends its capital works program: analysis of the replacement of MR-73 cars, extension of their service life, bus priority measures, Réno-Infrastructures phase 4, surface building repairs, and management of technological and security risks.

City council asks Québec to study the conditions for keeping in Montréal the tunnel boring machine used for the blue line. Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and LaSalle call for structuring public transit projects in the East and in the Greater Southwest, while Anjou asks the STM to stop the study of a reserved lane on rue Beaubien and avenue du Val-d'Anjou.

aSurveiller.texte: Approval from the ministère des Affaires municipales expected in November 2026 for borrowings related to the MR-73 cars and surface building repairs.
Work on the Rielle ventilation plant, in Verdun, must continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer vacation, for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel; the work is expected to continue until March 2028.
The opening of the five new blue line stations is planned for 2031.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and lanes, and the bike-sharing system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City and boroughs are building and repairing bike lanes, regulating car traffic around them, and buying equipment for the BIXI system. Work affects the REV Lajeunesse, rue Saint-Jacques, avenue Christophe-Colomb and corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. The City is also settling its rent with Hydro-Québec for land used as bike paths and asking Québec for financial help for four new projects.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes spending of $100,000, taxes included, for de-icing salt and abrasives spread notably on bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is renting a mini sweeper with operator for spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide.

Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie imposes mandatory manoeuvres on motorists on avenue Christophe-Colomb and makes official the bike lanes between rue des Carrières and rue de Bellechasse. Outremont tables a draft by-law to turn a shared lane on avenue Lajoie into a one-way bike path, and Ville-Marie makes rue Saint-Jacques one-way eastbound between Peel and Robert-Bourassa for a section of the REV.

The City awards PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61, taxes included, for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with BIXI, then a contract of $394,851.17, taxes included, to Laser AMP for the steel bases of the stations. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Sud-Ouest each include the installation of a BIXI station in street and alley projects.

City council approves an agreement for $125,167.62, taxes included, for unpaid rent from 2014 to 2025 on Hydro-Québec land used for bike paths, parks and gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, starting January 1, 2026, for a strip of about 366 square metres used as a bike path in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial help from Québec
etapes.texte: The City authorizes the filing of four financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable to build bike lanes and sidewalks on rues de Champlain, Saint-Jacques, Guy and Laurier. It commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: The new traffic directions and lane assignments on rue Saint-Jacques, related to the REV, take effect on November 6, 2026.
The lease for the bike path leased from Hydro-Québec in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until December 31, 2035.
